A_target.statement:
Let $D_n$ be the number of [[Definition:Derangement|derangements]] of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle D_n = n! \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {k!}$
and $\dfrac {D_n} {n!} \to \dfrac 1 e$.

B_source.statement:
Let $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ be finite sets.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \card {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} = \sum_{\O \mathop \ne S \mathop \subseteq \set {1, \ldots, n} } \paren {-1}^{\card S + 1} \card {\bigcap_{i \mathop \in S} A_i}$

object_map.reformulation: Count permutations with at least one fixed point by inclusion-exclusion and subtract from n!.

validity_conditions: The intersection over S depends only on the size of S, which collapses the sum.
The limit is the tail of the exponential series at -1.
proof_plan:
Let $A_i$ be the set of permutations fixing $i$.
Then $D_n = n! - \card {\bigcup_i A_i}$.
For $\card S = k$, the permutations fixing every element of $S$ number $\paren {n - k}!$.

By the source result:
:$\displaystyle \card {\bigcup_i A_i} = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {-1}^{k + 1} \binom n k \paren {n - k}! = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {-1}^{k + 1} \frac {n!} {k!}$

Hence $D_n = n! \displaystyle \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {k!}$, and $\dfrac {D_n} {n!}$ is a partial sum of the series for $e^{-1}$.
{{qed}}
